items.title: Podcast: Cognitive tests at scale, for pennies
items.summary: Jev from TypeSafe AI answers a defined question about text with a probability. What happens when researchers put this unusual tool through cognitive tests designed for people? This short conversation follows the independent work on xanderpico.com: a trait-order result opposite to the first-impression pattern used for comparison, a conjunction judgment that changes with layout, and word-similarity rankings that resemble human ratings while the raw scores do not. The hosts turn those results into practical advice for builders: pin the version and exact question, test wording, order and layout, compare with human ratings where available, and keep inactive inputs separate. The article and linked result write-ups have the full methods, numbers and caveats. Independent work; not affiliated with or endorsed by TypeSafe. This episode uses scripted AI-generated hosts and synthetic voices.

items.title: Thread: Cognitive tests at scale, for pennies
items.summary: Where do the quick judgments of a very cheap AI differ from ours, and what does running thousands of tests teach us about minds and about building with AI? Jev, from TypeSafe AI, answers a typed question about a text with a probability in about a fifth of a second for about two thousandths of a cent, and when it is confident it gives the same answer each time. That makes psychology-style experiments practical at a scale that normally needs hundreds of volunteers: rating thousands of words, or running a battery of classic bias tests in minutes. What turns up matters to AI builders, Jev users and brain researchers: some human quirks appear, some do not, and on first impressions it does the opposite of people.
